decisionGap: A reader who has heard 'harvest your losses' cannot tell from the headline how much a loss is worth (it depends on the rate on the gains it cancels, including 0%), how the $3,000 limit and carryforward work, that the technique defers tax rather than erasing it, or that buying the same fund in an IRA can void the loss. The existing wash-sale guide explains the 30-day rule in depth but not the how-much/when-it-pays question.
method: Calculated: a deterministic worked-arithmetic script (evidence/tax-loss-harvesting/run.py) applies the IRS-published $3,000 net-loss limit, the 0/15/20% long-term rates and the 2026 0%-bracket ceilings (Rev. Proc. 2025-32) to illustrative loss amounts, plus the IRS Pub. 550 wash-sale example. Rules are reported from IRS sources fetched 2026-11-04.

provenance.scopeAndLimits: Federal income tax, taxable accounts, US filers. Dollar amounts in the examples are illustrative, not any reader's result. Ordinary-income rates, state tax, net investment income tax and AMT are not modeled. The page does not claim we tested a harvesting product.

findings.claim: Net capital loss beyond gains: deduct the lesser of $3,000 ($1,500 married filing separately) or the net loss against other income; the remainder carries forward
findings.label: reported

findings.claim: 2026 long-term rates: 0% up to $49,450 taxable income (single, married filing separately), $66,200 (head of household) and $98,900 (married filing jointly), tested on taxable income including the gain; 15% up to $545,500 / $613,700 / $306,850
findings.label: reported

findings.claim: Wash sale: loss disallowed if substantially identical stock or securities are bought within 30 days before or after the sale, including in an IRA or Roth IRA; disallowed loss is added to the new shares' basis and the holding period carries over
findings.label: reported

findings.claim: $10,000 harvested loss against $10,000 of long-term gain saves $0 / $1,500 / $2,000 of federal tax at 0% / 15% / 20%
findings.label: calculated

findings.claim: $10,000 net loss with no gains: $3,000 deducted ($1,500 MFS), $7,000 carried forward
findings.label: calculated

findings.claim: Deferral: a $3,000 harvested loss resets basis to the new purchase price, so selling later at the original price realizes the same $3,000 gain
findings.label: calculated

finding: Tax loss harvesting is worth the tax rate on the gains the loss cancels (nothing if those gains would be taxed at 0%), the first $3,000 a year of any excess loss also reduces other income, the rest carries forward, and the benefit is mostly a deferral because the replacement shares start at a lower basis. A purchase of the same or a substantially identical security within 30 days before or after the sale, in any of your accounts including an IRA, disallows the loss.
conditions: Federal rules, taxable accounts, US taxpayers. The benefit disappears if the offset gains are taxed at 0% (taxable income including the gain at or below $49,450 single or married filing separately, $66,200 head of household, $98,900 married filing jointly in 2026), if the replacement purchase triggers the wash-sale rule, or if the investor never realizes the deferred gain at a higher rate. Not tax advice.
whatWouldChange: A change to the IRS loss limit, the 2026 rate thresholds, or the wash-sale rule; for an individual, a different taxable-income bracket or a state-tax rule.
decisionChangingCounterexample: At a 0% long-term rate the $10,000 loss saves $0 against gains; with no gains the deduction is capped at $3,000 and the rest waits.
counterexample: Reader in the 0% long-term bracket: harvesting $10,000 of losses against $10,000 of long-term gains saves $0 in federal tax that year (run.py: 0pct = 0.0); a reader who rebuys the same fund inside 30 days or in an IRA loses the deduction altogether (IRS Pub. 550 example 1: $250 loss disallowed, basis $1,050).
limitations: Illustrative inputs; federal only; short-term gains are taxed at ordinary rates (not modeled); NIIT, state taxes and transaction costs are not modeled; the deferral has exceptions (a 0% year, step-up at death, gift to charity).
unknowns: Any reader's own taxable income, basis or holdings
Which replacement funds an IRS reviewer would call substantially identical (no mechanical IRS test; Pub. 550 says facts and circumstances)
selectedMedium: text with one worked-arithmetic table (loss amount x long-term rate) and one 'what would change this' section; no calculator because /stock-capital-gains-tax-calculator/ already computes sale-specific tax and a harvest depends on the reader's holdings
takeaway: For a US taxpayer with realized capital gains taxed at 15% or 20%, harvesting a loss saves 15 or 20 cents of federal tax per dollar of loss now; with gains taxed at 0% it saves nothing, and with no gains it saves tax only on the first $3,000 a year. Applies to taxable accounts, not IRAs. Evidence basis: IRS rules (reported) plus our worked arithmetic (calculated). Changes if you buy the same or a substantially identical security within the 30-day windows, or if a higher future rate makes the deferral costly. Next step: list your realized gains and losses for 2026 on the IRS worksheet and, before selling, confirm no repurchase falls inside the window.
